scenes.title: Envelope Fourteen-AB Returns
scenes.summary: At four in the afternoon on Tuesday, M4 returns from the Municipal Archive Vault carrying the sealed manila packet holding both 1890 wrought-iron keys.
scenes.intro: Four chimes ring softly across {CITY} on Tuesday afternoon as {M4} strides into the lobby of {SHOW} holding a heavy wax-stamped Municipal Vault packet before {F1} and {M2}. Listen first.
story: M2
{M4}! Tell me the vault clerk accepted both signatures and our five-digit tally code!
M4
Verified every digit against the nineteen-sixty-six ledger and brought this up from Basement Three!
F1
Feel the weight of that canvas-lined envelope—sixty years in dry municipal storage!
M2
Slide open the brass clasp carefully, {M4}, while my glasses sit squarely in place!
M4
Out come two identical twenty-centimetre wrought-iron keys with three-leaf clover bows!
F1
Not a speck of red rust anywhere—look at the engraved brass tags attached!
M4
Left tag reads Plot Fourteen-A West Courtyard; right tag reads Plot Fourteen-B East Courtyard.
M2
Look at the symmetrical three-pronged wards cut into the iron bit—pure nineteenth-century artistry!
F1
Wait—we promised Number Twelve we would deliver her East Key before half past four!
M4
So both households can stand on opposite sides of the oak door at five sharp!
M2
Leave our West Key with {M1} right now so he prepares the lock cylinder!
F1
And {F2} and I will carry the East Key next door on a silver tray!
scenes.outro: Two clover-bowed iron keys gleam side by side after sixty silent years underground! See you outside next time.

scenes.title: Delivering the East Key
scenes.summary: Stepping back from House Number Twelve at half past four, F1, F2, and M4 celebrate seeing the restored six-tile porcelain sign already hanging beside their neighbour's gate.
scenes.intro: Out on sunny {STREET} ten minutes later, {F1}, {F2}, and {M4} pause happily between both gates after delivering the East Key next door. Let us listen in first.
story: F2
Look beside Number Twelve and her green gate—she already hung our cedar tile frame!
M4
Twin Courtyards Kiln and Bakehouse looks as if it never left that limestone wall!
F1
Did you see how tightly she held that clover-bowed iron key when we handed it over?
F2
She said her father spoke about the sunlit conservatory every winter of her childhood!
M4
And she confirmed the five-sharp signal: three clear knocks from our side first.
F1
Followed by three answering knocks from her courtyard before both keys turn together!
F2
Just in case sixty-year-old hinges groan loudly, I brewed a big pot of mint tea.
M4
Good thinking, Chef—historic dust makes thirsty work for seven curious neighbours.
F1
Wait—did {M1} say the star keyhole needed cleaning before five chimes strike?
M4
He is kneeling behind the rosemary shelves right now with a goose-feather brush!
F2
Go hold the tray for {M1}, {F1}, while {M4} and I bring lanterns!
F1
Twenty minutes until five—our courtyard wall is about to grow a whole room!
scenes.outro: The cobalt sign shines outside Number Twelve, and a three-knock signal is set for five sharp! See you by the arch next time.

scenes.title: Graphite in the Star Lock
scenes.summary: At quarter to five behind the rosemary wall, M1 teaches F1 why dry powdered graphite—never sticky grease—belongs inside a century-old iron lock.
scenes.intro: Kneeling on a folded canvas mat before the 1890 stone arch, {M1} puffs fine grey graphite powder into the star-shaped keyhole while {F1} holds the West Key ready. Listen first.
story: F1
Why are you puffing dry grey pencil powder instead of warm oil this time, {M1}?
M1
Liquid oil inside an outdoor iron lock collects grit until the tumblers gum shut.
F1
Whereas dry powdered graphite coats the iron wards slick as ice without trapping dust!
M1
You have been paying perilous amounts of attention to my maintenance lectures, {F1}.
F1
Someone has to preserve fifteen years of handyman wisdom at {SHOW}, right?
M1
Now slide the West Key straight in until the shoulder kisses the escutcheon plate.
F1
Oh, feel how smoothly all three iron prongs passed the inner ward collar!
M1
Do not turn it yet—just test two millimetres of spring tension to the left.
F1
The internal spring still pushes back crisply after sixty years without a single turn!
M1
Whoever forged this lock in eighteen-ninety tempered steel springs properly over charcoal.
F1
Listen—footsteps in our courtyard; everyone is gathering behind table one for five!
M1
Leave the key in the slot and step back—the clock tower is ready.
scenes.outro: Dry graphite and charcoal-tempered steel stand poised as the clock hands near five sharp! See you next time.

scenes.title: Three Knocks Through the Oak
scenes.summary: As five chimes echo down {STREET}, M1 raps three times on the 1890 oak door, three clear knocks answer from Number Twelve, and both deadbolts slide free!
scenes.intro: Five bronze chimes drift across {CITY} in the golden late afternoon. Around the 1890 stone arch behind the rosemary wall, {F1}, {M1}, and {M2} hold their breath. Listen to the whole scene first.
story: M2
Chime five has faded—knock politely on the centre oak stile, {M1}!
M1
One firm knock, two firm knocks, three firm knocks... now everybody stay completely quiet.
F1
TAP, TAP, TAP! Three clear knocks just answered right through the seasoned oak!
M2
My goosebumps have goosebumps! Turn the West Key counterclockwise slowly, {M1}!
M1
Turning firmly left... half turn... full turn... hear that heavy lower deadbolt retract?!
F1
CLUNK! And listen above it—the upper East Bolt is sliding back from her side!
M2
Both opposing deadbolts are clear for the first time since nineteen-sixty-six!
M1
Hold the brass lantern high, {F1}, while I ease the iron ring inward.
F1
Wait—does this door swing toward our courtyard or inward into the conservatory?
M1
Inward on concealed parliament hinges... zero scraping, cool dry air rushing out!
M2
Smell that air: baked terracotta clay, dried lavender, and clean old lime plaster!
F1
Step across the threshold together—look up at that arched glass ceiling!
scenes.outro: Two opposing bolts retract in harmony, and sixty years of sealed twilight swing gently open! See you inside the vault next time.

scenes.title: Under the Cobalt Vault
scenes.summary: Stepping inside the forgotten 1890 conservatory gallery, F1, M2, and M3 marvel at the vaulted iron-and-glass roof, cobalt wall tiles, and friendly wave across the room.
scenes.intro: Slanting Tuesday sunlight filters through dusty overhead glass ribs into a three-metre-wide vaulted gallery linking both historic houses. {F1}, {M2}, and {M3} step softly onto patterned geometric floor tiles. Let us listen in first.
story: M3
Look at those curved wrought-iron roof ribs springing from glazed cobalt brick pilasters!
F1
It is twelve metres long from front to back—a hidden glass street between two courtyards!
M2
And look across the eastern oak doorway—our neighbour is waving her lantern warmly!
F1
Wave back, {M2}! Look how both arched doorways mirror each other stone for stone!
M3
On our west wall sits a recessed ceramic bread-warming chamber lined with soapstone shelves.
M2
And opposite on her east wall stands an antique porcelain-glazing bench with tile racks!
F1
Wait—why is the air in here so temperate and pleasant without any radiator?
M3
Thermal mass! Thick brick party walls store daytime sun trapped beneath the overhead glass.
M2
No wonder the National Guidebook Editor remembered hearing legends about an eighteen-ninety arch!
F1
Once we wash a century of dust off those glass panes, this vault will blaze!
M3
Before anyone celebrates, look straight down at the centre of the mosaic floor.
M2
Is that a porcelain basin catching water right on the middle boundary line?!
scenes.outro: Wrought-iron ribs and cobalt brick dazzle every eye—right down to a porcelain bowl catching a sixty-year drip! See you next time.

scenes.title: The Mosaic Boundary Line
scenes.summary: Exploring the bakery side of the vaulted gallery, F2, F3, and M3 spot the mosaic centre line and uncover four carved 1890 terracotta bread stamps inside the hearth drawer.
scenes.intro: Joining {M3} inside the vaulted glass gallery, {F2} and {F3} kneel beside the cobalt-tiled bread-warming alcove on the western wall. Listen first.
story: F2
Oh, {F3}, look at this domed ceramic warming oven—built to keep forty loaves warm!
F3
And look at the tiny cream-and-blue mosaic line running straight down the floor!
M3
West of that blue line belongs to {SHOW}; east belongs to Number Twelve.
F2
Wait—pull open that lower iron drawer beneath the soapstone shelf gently, {M3}!
M3
Slides right out on iron runners—and four round terracotta medallions are resting inside!
F3
Brush the fine dust off the carved face with your linen napkin, {F2}.
F2
Look at the relief carving: a golden wheat sheaf intertwined with a musical lyre!
F3
Bread stamps! Nineteenth-century bakers pressed those medallions into risen dough before baking!
M3
Notice how the fourth stamp shows a ceramic amphora beside the wheat sheaf too!
F2
Proof in solid clay that both houses shared festival loaves long before that plum tart!
F3
If you bake braided cardamom loaves stamped with these medallions on Friday, {F2}...
F2
The guidebook photographer will smell eighteen-ninety before even clicking the camera shutter!
scenes.outro: Four carved terracotta bread stamps unite wheat, music, and pottery in a single 1890 crest! See you next time.

scenes.title: Tracing the Skylight Drip
scenes.summary: Looking upward from the centre of the gallery, M1, M3, and F1 find one cracked glass pane high in the skylight ridge that needs reglazing from the upper ladder.
scenes.intro: Standing beside the shallow porcelain bowl near the middle of the floor, {M1}, {M3}, and {F1} tilt their heads up toward the arched glass skylight five metres overhead. Listen first.
story: F1
Good thing someone left this wide stoneware bowl here before locking the doors!
M1
Dry summers evaporated whatever winter rain dripped through that single hairline crack above.
M3
Third ridge pane from the north, {M1}—forty centimetres wide by sixty centimetres long.
M1
Six-millimetre wired horticultural glass set in linseed putty along T-bar iron ribs.
F1
Can you reach that ridge safely without standing on the glass vault itself, {M1}?
M1
Easily: we lay my padded roof-plank across the brick parapets from our upper balcony.
M3
I can order a custom six-millimetre clear glass pane cut first thing Wednesday morning!
F1
While you two reglaze the ridge tomorrow, {F2} and I can wash the lower panes!
M1
Hold on—check the brick flue above the bread warmer while we are looking up.
M3
Capped cleanly with a copper cowl, and the soapstone chamber uses hot-water thermal bricks!
F1
Hot bricks heated in our kitchen oven and slid inside—zero smoke anywhere!
M1
Smartest nineteenth-century room on {STREET}; let us go tell the boss the repair list.
scenes.outro: One custom pane of glass and zero smoke flues make Wednesday's restoration plan crystal clear! Final scene of Episode 3!

scenes.title: The Sepia Postcard of 1905
scenes.summary: At the front desk Tuesday night, F1, M2, and F3 admire a 1905 sepia photograph lent by their Room 5 postmaster showing one communal table spanning both halves of the glass gallery.
scenes.intro: Back at the warm front desk on Tuesday evening, {F1}, {M2}, and {F3} lean over a crisp 1905 sepia postcard photograph left beside the ledger by their Room 5 archivist guest. Listen first.
story: F3
Oh, look what our thoughtful postmaster in Room Five slipped onto the blotter!
F1
A real nineteen-oh-five sepia photograph taken right inside our vaulted glass conservatory!
M2
Glasses on my nose—twenty smiling neighbours seated along one enormous wooden table!
F3
Notice where the table legs stand, {M2}: straddling straight across the mosaic boundary line!
F1
Hanging ferns overhead, teacups in every hand, and both courtyard oak doors wide open!
M2
Magnificent... although speaking strictly as an insured property owner, straddling boundaries sounds legally complex!
F3
{M2}, please tell me you are not planning to divide a winter garden in half!
M2
Not a brick wall, {F3}—merely a discreet, orderly visual boundary marker for clarity!
F1
Uh-oh, whenever {M2} says discreet visual marker, hide the paintbrushes and the chalk!
M2
Sleep soundly, ladies; Wednesday morning begins our grand conservatory transformation!
F3
Remind {M1} to guard the mosaic floor at eight sharp tomorrow morning, {F1}.
F1
Written at the top of the Wednesday page—see you under the glass vault at dawn!
scenes.outro: A 1905 sepia banquet inspires everyone—while {M2} quietly plots a boundary line of his own! End of Episode 3—see you in Episode 4!
